note: Non-stick by design. Untreated PTFE needs a silicone adhesive, or chemically etched PTFE for acrylic tapes.
Only silicone adhesives wet it reliably. Silicone oils in the part can also migrate and weaken other bonds.
The classic hard-to-bond plastic. Glass-filled and talc-filled grades behave differently: test the actual grade.
Polyolefin based, so treat as low surface energy (3M lists TPO among the LSE plastics).
Slick, crystalline surface: test both a standard and an LSE acrylic.
Prone to stress cracking from solvents; clean with isopropyl alcohol and water, not stronger solvents.
Flexible PVC contains plasticizers that migrate into many adhesives and soften them; ask for a plasticizer-resistant adhesive.
Absorbs moisture; dry parts bond differently from parts that have sat in humid storage.
Varies widely with the formulation (3M: "broad range"); tesa lists powder coatings with the low-energy surfaces. Measure with dyne pens and test.
High energy when clean, but rolling oil and oxide films are common: clean before bonding.
Stainless steel is the reference surface in most peel tests, so datasheet peel values are measured on it.
